Based on the provided context, here is a Semgrep rule that matches the vulnerable code structure:

```yaml
rules:
- id: "vuln-fate-6feccf6d"
  pattern: $FUNC(...).remove_sensitive_info(...)
  pattern-not: $FUNC(...).remove_sensitive_info("trusted_tree")
  languages: ["python"]
  message: |
    Potential sensitive information exposure detected. The remove_sensitive_info method is used to remove sensitive information from the tree. This could lead to unauthorized access to sensitive data.
    To fix this, ensure that the remove_sensitive_info method is only called with trusted data.
  severity: ERROR
  metadata:
    source-url: github.com/FederatedAI/FATE/commit/6feccf6d752184a6f9365d56a76fe627983e7139
    category: security
    cwe: [relevant CWE number]
    owasp: [relevant OWASP category]
    references: [links to documentation or standards]
    technology: python
```

This rule will match any call to `remove_sensitive_info` method on an object of any class. The `pattern-not` field is used to exclude calls to `remove_sensitive_info` with a string argument "trusted_tree".

Please replace `[relevant CWE number]`, `[relevant OWASP category]`, `[links to documentation or standards]` with the relevant CWE number, OWASP category, and references to documentation or standards.

Please note that this rule is a general one and might not cover all the variations of the same issue. You might need to adapt it to match the specific vulnerability in the patch.
